_comment: Permission grant for the unattended Saturday 09:00 weekly-agent-review run
(.github/workflows/scheduled-tasks.yml). Passed with `claude --settings`, which MERGES with
the host's settings rather than replacing them.
WHY A SEPARATE FILE FROM daily-triage-permissions.json: the two runs need almost nothing in
common. The triage acts on the outside world — it drafts mail, opens draft PRs, places chat
messages — and its allowlist is shaped around bounding that. This run only reads local state
(~/agent-memory routing and session logs, this repo's git history, open GitHub issues and PRs)
and writes exactly one artifact: a decision record, through tools/decision-log.js. Reusing the
triage's list would hand a read-only reviewer the ability to send messages and draft mail for
no reason. Same argument as #203 against --dangerously-skip-permissions: unattended is exactly
where the blast radius matters most, so the grant is an allowlist in git, reviewable in a diff.
WRITE AND EDIT ARE DENIED, NOT MERELY UNLISTED. A weekly review that quietly starts editing the
repo at 09:00 on a Saturday is the failure mode worth engineering against: nobody is watching,
and the next person to pull sees changes with no PR behind them. Deny rules take precedence
over allow, so this holds even if the prompt or a future skill asks for an edit. The review's
one output is the decision record, and it goes through `node tools/decision-log.js --write`,
which lands in ~/agent-memory (a separate, private repo) rather than in this checkout.
NO MCP CONNECTORS. The inputs are all local files and `gh`. Granting Gmail/Calendar/Drive/Notion
here would widen the surface for data this review never reads.
`gh` STAYS USABLE for the read half of the review — open `human-needed` alerts, stale PRs, issue
age — with the state-changing subcommands denied. Merging is Sam's gate and a human's call; it
is not something an unattended weekly reviewer should be able to reach at all.
